newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: HSBC HOPES FOR 20 PCT RETURN A YEAR IN ARGENTINA.
newsitem.headline: HSBC HOPES FOR 20 PCT RETURN A YEAR IN ARGENTINA.

text.p: HSBC's Keith Whitson said Friday the group hopes for a 20 percent return on equity for the $600-$700 million it will pay for Argentine financial services holding company Grupo Roberts.

"Our group as a whole is currently recording returns in excess of 20 percent per annum on equity," the chief executive of Midland Bank and chairman of banking giant HSBC's Latin American unit told a press conference in Buenos Aires.
"That is an indication of the sort of level of return we will eventually be able to receive in Argentina," he said. Nevertheless, he added that "a lot, of course, will depend on external conditions."

HSBC Holdings Plc, considered the world largest financial services group, announced in May the purchase of Grupo Roberts in the latest of a string of deals in Latin America, where it also has interests in Brazil, Mexico, Chile and Peru.
Whitson said HSBC regards Latin America and Asia as the two areas of the world which are likely to witness the most impressive growth in the forseeable future.
In 1992 it acquired Midland Bank in what was at the time the world's largest single banking merger.
"We said at that particular time that it would probably take us aproximately four years to digest the Midland acquisition," Whitson said.
"That has gone very succesfully and about the middle of last year we started to look towards Latin America more seriously."
Whitson said Argentina's Central Bank gave HSBC Thursday formal approval for the acquisiton of Roberts. He expects it to be signed within the next few days.

He also said HSBC has concluded a transaction in Brazil to buy 100 percent of Bamerindus, the country's fourth largest bank, and was giving the final touches to buy slighlty less than 20 percent of Mexico's Grupo Financiero Serfin.
Whitson said Bamerindus acquisiton was a major deal but quite different from that of Grupo Roberts, as the Brazilian bank underwent significant difficulties and was intervened by the central bank.

"Opportunities don't always come along when one would like them too, but in this particular case we belive that we have been extremely fortunate to be able to expand in Brazil and Argentina" over a short period of time.
Whitson said Grupo Roberts's bank, Banco Roberts, was a "first class" one with good management.
Enrique Ruete, President of Grupo Roberts executive committe, will assume as chairman of Grupo Roberts, Whitson ssaid. Michael Smith takes respoonsibility as executive director.
Whitson said he hoped other senior directors and managers of Grupo Roberts will continue to work with HSBC.
HSBC announced Monday record first half profits of 2.6 billion pound sterling, 13 percent higher than in the same period year ago, Whitson said.
Banco Roberts Thursday announced a yearly net gain of $28 million, net worth of $283.7 million and retained earnings of $61.4 million.
